name: Comgrow Z1 5W
tagline: 5W Budget Comgrow diode: often bundled with 3D printer deals
tldr: Comgrow Z1 5W is the 5W SKU on the Comgrow comgrow z1 line. Comgrow's Z1 targets entry-level buyers, often sold alongside Ender 3D printers. Verify optical power on the listing: do not assume combined-watt marketing.
mainObjective: Detailed engraving on organics and coated metal: occasional thin cuts only

priceRange.note: 5W optical module: verify SKU before buying

engraveExample.description: Filled photo or logo on birch plywood

cutExample.description: Simple square cut-out from 3 mm basswood

pros: Lowest price of the Z1 line: $179–249
Finest spot of the three tiers in our profile (~0.08 mm): fine for text, logos and line art
Low power keeps smoke and charring modest on leather, card and thin wood
cons: Very slow photo fills: ~28–43 min for our 10 × 10 cm test, at 2–4 mm/s
Cutting is limited to thin stock: a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes ~14–24 min in our benchmark
No acrylic cutting in practice, and no path to thick wood without replacing the module
beginnerNotes: This profile is the 5W SKU on Comgrow Z1. Read the TL;DR and benchmarks above, then compare other power options via the chips before buying.
proTips: Optimize for engraving: lower DPI on photos, higher scan speed on line art after test burns. Air assist still helps clarity. Compare benchmark times on the next tier before assuming you need more power.
primaryUse: Engraving-first desktop diode for makers who prioritize mark quality over cut speed

editorialDepth.advantages: Comgrow Z1 5W suits makers who sell marks, photos, and gifts more than daily panel cutting. Reasonable open-frame entry price.
editorialDepth.limitations: Skip if you already quote 4 mm+ cutting in production: see 10W or 20W in the line. Not for cast acrylic or bare metal without spray.

faq.question: What can the Comgrow Z1 5W realistically cut?
faq.answer: Paper, card, fabric and thin basswood, with several passes from about 3 mm. Comgrow does not publish a per-thickness cutting chart; in our benchmark a 10 × 10 cm square in 3 mm basswood takes ~14–24 min at 2–3 mm/s. Anything thicker belongs on a higher-watt machine.

faq.question: How long does a photo engraving take on the Z1 5W?
faq.answer: Plan on ~28–43 min for a 10 × 10 cm filled photo on birch plywood in our benchmark, against ~18–28 min on the 10W. For line art and text the gap is smaller, since outlines use far less laser time than fills.

faq.question: Is the 5W enough for a beginner, or should I start with the 10W?
faq.answer: The 5W is enough if you want to learn and engrave small gifts on a tight budget ($179–249). If you already know you want to cut ornaments or puzzles, the 10W ($219–299) costs about $40 more and saves a third of the time on both cutting and engraving.

standoutFeatures.title: Lowest entry price
standoutFeatures.body: $179–249, the cheapest way into the Comgrow Z1 platform and its LightBurn and LaserGRBL support.

standoutFeatures.title: Finest spot of the line
standoutFeatures.body: ~0.08 mm spot in our profile, slightly tighter than the 10W and 20W modules, which suits text and line work.
